key_insight: GRC frames learning as recursively closing residual errors so an agent can both preserve prior responsibilities and remain able to learn new ones.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a stability-plasticity criterion and update rule that are relevant for designing adaptive constitutive models and other systems that must revise representations without breaking prior behavior.
method: Defines a complete representation-relation view at a fixed learner-world boundary.
Separates internal learning into transformation within a representation versus revision of the representation.
Derives an affine constrained quadratic update with a unique safe-response solution and a criterion for when revision is required.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations, local tangent decomposition, necessary-and-sufficient conditions, and proofs rather than experimental or dataset-based evaluation.
watch_item: The framework relies on regularity and affine-model assumptions, so practical use may depend on whether a real system can satisfy or approximate those conditions.
paper_title: Generalized Residual Closure: General Learning Dynamics for Stability-Plasticity Compatibility
